projects.title: Non-invasive Brain Computer Interface for a Exoskeleton
projects.description: I worked on an EMG based brain computer interface to control an exoskeleton designed to reduce the risk of lifting related injuries in light industrial environments.  This device is designed to be safely operated by industrial workers with less than an hour of device specific training. The proof of concept we built consisted of a motorized frame for the elbow joint with the EMG interface.

projects.title: Computer Architecture Class Project - RISC-V System On a Chip
projects.description:
Built a RISC-V System on a Chip that used the RV32I ISA. The design had to be possible to flash onto a Zynq Z7020 FPGA. All of the circuits that were flashed in that chip were designed by us except for the clock multiplier which was provided on the FPGA. We also designed test fixtures for each subcomponent and used test driven development methodologies to detect and remove bugs in our circuit design.

This was done for a Computer Architecture class that was in development at the time. Because of this we helped to adapt labs from our computer architecture textbook to run in a real FPGA and not just a simulator.
